parameters.name: GND back-stress strengthening contribution at necking (AN850-T)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Initial AN850-T phase fractions (F 54.7%, B/TM 41.4%, FM 3.3%, RA 0.6%); phase sizes (F 5.35 µm, B/TM 0.86 µm, FM 0.40 µm, RA 0.83 µm); initial dislocation densities from Table A2; DIM average size c = 0.19 µm; R = 1.44 µm, Δh = 4.33 µm; constitutive parameters in Table A2.
computational_details.simulation_method: Phase mechanical response constitutive model combining iso-work theory and von Mises equivalent method; Mecking-Kocks dislocation evolution; Olson-Cohen TRIP kinetics; back stress from GND density gradient
computational_details.software_used: AZtecCrystal (Parent Grain Analysis module; Huang et al. reconstruction algorithm)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Model aligns closely with experimental true stress–true strain curves; model values are higher at the initial strain stage; for AN850-T the lower RA content results in no significant DIM-induced strain hardening.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: GND accumulation and back stress at soft/hard phase boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: KAM reaches its peak when characteristic lines cross F/B-TM boundaries (AN850-T KAM_AVE = 0.62°); point-to-point misorientation spikes and Kikuchi-pattern-quality minima coincide with phase interfaces (AN850-T P-T-P_AVE = 3.50); back stress at necking reported as 278 MPa (maximum stress from σ_B) and 254 MPa (GND back-stress strengthening contribution).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: micropore nucleation at soft/hard domain interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Microscale voids are mainly distributed at soft/hard domain interfaces; white-pixel regions in EBSD maps mark sites prone to micropore nucleation and expansion.

interfaces.interface_notes: In AN850-T, hard domains were severed during fracture (carbon/manganese oversaturation at 850 °C increased strength but brittleness of hard domains).
interfaces.phase_evolution: RA transforms into deformation-induced martensite (DIM) via the TRIP effect during deformation; AN850-T RA before deformation 0.6%, final DIM ≈ 0.28%, and RA after fracture ≈ 0.2%.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Coordinated deformation between soft ferrite and hard B/TM/FM domains: internal compressive stress in F weakens tensile-load promotion of dislocation motion (soft-domain hardening), while adjacent hard domains experience tensile-direction internal stress (hard-domain softening), maintaining deformation continuity.

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: 2–3 times higher yield strength than conventional low-alloy high-strength steels; mechanical properties comparable to advanced high-strength steel

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 39 kg low-density steel ingot with composition Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si-0.009S-0.009P was produced via vacuum induction melting.
The ingot was hot forged and cut into billets measuring 90 mm (length) x 70 mm (width) x 40 mm (thickness).
Billets heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolling on a high-rigidity two-roll mill, beginning at 1100 °C; six passes; cumulative reduction 90%; final thickness 4 mm; finish rolling at 880 °C followed by air cooling.
Cold rolling on a four-roll reversible mill with 60% reduction, resulting in plates 1.6 mm thick.
Cold-rolled samples annealed at 850 °C for 30 min within the critical region and air-cooled to room temperature; labeled AN850.

Holding in the lower bainite region at 400 °C for 30 min; produced sample designated AN850-T. Aging in the lower bainite region refines bainitic structures, controls bainite transformation kinetics and prevents pearlite formation.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Instron 3382; load applied parallel to rolling direction (RD); three specimens per group; DIC images captured every 2 s

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase heterogeneous microstructure composed of ferrite (F), bainite (B), tempered martensite (TM), fresh martensite (FM), and retained austenite (RA); hard phases (B/TM, FM, and deformation-induced martensite) decorate ferrite grain boundaries.

unmapped_findings: AN850-T retained austenite (RA) content before deformation was 0.6%, and after tensile fracture the austenite fraction decreased to 0.002 (0.2%) (b0036, figure_012).
During tensile deformation AN850-T transformed retained austenite into deformation-induced martensite (DIM), reaching a final DIM fraction of about 0.28% (figure_007).
AN850-T showed a broadened DIC strain-concentration band during deformation, with no second local strain-concentration annotation unlike AN800-T (figure_009).

At 850 °C, significant migration of carbon and manganese into the B/TM and FM regions resulted in local oversaturation of alloying elements, increasing strength but also brittleness of the hard domains; in AN850-T the hard domains were severed during fracture (b0131).

AN850-T fracture surface showed dimples plus quasi-cleavage regions, mostly originating from fresh martensite; the dimple size distribution was bimodal (average 1.31 µm, Peak I 0.60 µm, Peak II 1.78 µm) (b0131, figure_011).
For AN850-T, the lower retained austenite content resulted in no significant strain-hardening phenomenon induced by DIM (b0128).
The B/TM strength contribution reached 54% of the flow stress at necking strain for AN850-T, the highest among the three tempered samples (b0128).
No dynamic propagation instabilities such as Lüders bands or Portevin-Le Chatelier bands were observed in any of the samples (b0044).
